arXiv.title: Improvements in the contemporary implementation of photoemission spectroscopy
arXiv.abstract: In this short communication, we refined our previous manuscript to illustrate the corrections needed to the prevalent method for determining photoelectron counts in modern MCP-CCD-based ARPES detector systems and to implement our proposed 'new' photoelectron-detection method therein. We therefore provide a simple, practical solution for verifying changes in the ARPES spectrum using the 'new' method in modern ARPES spectrometers. The solution is simple enough to enable both the 'old' and 'new' methods within a single spectrometer, allowing a direct and rapid comparison of ARPES spectra collected under otherwise identical experimental conditions. We thus conclude our proposal.

arXiv.title: LT@Helsinki at SemEval-2020 Task 12: Multilingual or language-specific BERT?
arXiv.comments: Accepted at SemEval-2020 Task 12. Identical to camera-ready version except where adjustments to fit arXiv requirements were necessary
arXiv.abstract: This paper presents the different models submitted by the LT@Helsinki team for the SemEval 2020 Shared Task 12. Our team participated in sub-tasks A and C; titled offensive language identification and offense target identification, respectively. In both cases we used the so-called Bidirectional Encoder Representation from Transformer (BERT), a model pre-trained by Google and fine-tuned by us on the OLID and SOLID datasets. The results show that offensive tweet classification is one of several language-based tasks where BERT can achieve state-of-the-art results.
